title: The Vector of Sector Nine
premise: On the fringe colony of Sector Nine, Paloma Thackeray investigates 'impossible accidents' while quietly maintaining an ancient beacon whose original purpose has been erased from every record. When the colony's children begin sharing one dream — a countdown, a star map, a voice calling itself the Vector — Paloma discovers the beacon is a dormant archive from the war's first days, holding proof that Sector Nine's ruling Consortium manufactured the enemy attack that justified their power. As Consortium enforcers close in and the children's dream begins rewriting their memories, Paloma must choose between erasing the beacon to keep her found family safe or broadcasting its message, which will end the war by exposing everyone who profited from it. In the end she broadcasts it, sacrificing her own recorded memories of the people she loves so the truth can survive without her.
about_author: Yara Galloway is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years on remote stations where the only company was static and old transmissions. She writes science fiction about the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Paloma Thackeray, insurance investigator for Sector Nine Colony, examines a cargo lift failure that killed no one but moved a shipment no manifest lists. Her POV establishes her methodical loneliness and her private ritual: climbing to the ridge each night to service a beacon no file admits exists. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking isolation.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Paloma cross-references the lift incident against a decade of impossible accidents and finds they form a perimeter around the beacon's coordinates. POV alternates with twelve-year-old Idris Okonkwo, who sketches the same spiral in his schoolbook without knowing why. Emotional beat: unease — the colony is arranged around something forgotten on purpose.

chapters.title: The Children's Dream
chapters.summary: Seven children report identical dreams: a countdown, a red star, a voice saying 'deliver us.' Idris's POV dominates; his mother dismisses it as fever. Paloma interviews him for an unrelated claim and recognizes the spiral from the beacon's casing. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Consortium Attention
chapters.summary: Deputy Administrator Voss requests all of Paloma's accident files — politely, which is worse than a subpoena. Paloma's POV; she hides the beacon log inside an insurance archive. Meanwhile the children's dream gains a new element: a name, half-spoken. Emotional beat: the first true sense of being watched.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma opens the beacon's maintenance hatch and finds a second mechanism beneath her own additions — an archive core, still warm after decades. Her POV, interwoven with fragmented archive audio in italics. She realizes someone built it to be found by exactly one kind of person: an investigator. Emotional beat: awe and vertigo.

chapters.title: Found Family, Small Hours
chapters.summary: A quieter chapter: dinner at the Okonkwos', where Paloma is unofficially family — Idris, his grandmother Ama, mechanic Sefa, and retired teacher Brin. The children compare dreams at the table. Paloma almost tells them about the beacon and doesn't. Emotional beat: warmth, and the cost of secrets kept for love.

chapters.title: Voss Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Voss visits Paloma's office, probing whether she's heard the children talk. His courtesy frays when she mentions the word 'beacon' casually, testing him. His micro-reaction confirms he knows what it is. Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: chess played with smiles.

chapters.title: The First Impossible Accident Repeats
chapters.summary: Sefa's workshop suffers a pressure blowout — same signature as the cargo lift. No deaths again, but this time the children were nearby, and afterward Idris can't remember his grandmother's maiden name. Idris's POV. Emotional beat: grief arriving before loss.

chapters.title: Archive Fragment One
chapters.summary: Paloma plays the first recoverable archive segment: a woman's voice, dated to the war's opening week, describing 'the false incursion at Meridian Gate.' The war that defined Sector Nine began with a lie. Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: the ground tilting under everything she believed.

chapters.title: Brin Knew Someone
chapters.summary: Retired teacher Brin admits that decades ago she taught a girl named Oyelaran — the voice on the archive — before the girl's family was 'relocated.' Brin has kept one letter hidden in a hymnal. Shared POV between Brin and Paloma. Emotional beat: memory as contraband.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: The letter names the beacon's builders: a cell of archivists who hid proof of the Consortium's fabricated attack, scattering keys among ordinary colonists. It warns: 'They will not kill you. They will make you forget why you should be afraid.' Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: inheritance of a dangerous duty.

chapters.title: Countdown Made Visible
chapters.summary: The children's dream synchronizes fully — all nine now see the same numbers, and the numbers match a decay timer Paloma finds in the archive core: ninety-one days until the beacon's data self-erases. Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: the clock starts in earnest.

chapters.title: Voss's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Voss offers Paloma a promotion off-world — generous, immediate, suspiciously tailored to her debts. Refusal will mark her. She stalls. Interlude from Voss's POV revealing he genuinely believes forgetting protects the colony. Emotional beat: the antagonist made human, which makes him worse.

chapters.title: Sefa Repairs More Than Machines
chapters.summary: Sefa discovers tampering in the colony's grid — deliberate memory-degrading harmonics in the power frequency, tuned to adults only. The children dream because their brains are untouched. Sefa's POV. Emotional beat: rage at a violence no one can feel happening.

chapters.title: The Night the Dream Spoke Back
chapters.summary: Idris answers the dream aloud, and the next morning the beacon transmits a single line to Paloma's handheld: 'WHO MAINTAINS ME?' Paloma answers honestly. Her POV, intimate and strange. Emotional beat: first contact with the thing she's tended.

chapters.title: Nine Keys
chapters.summary: The archive requires nine living memories to unlock broadcast capability — one per dreaming child, offered willingly. The Vector explains: memory freely given cannot be retracted or forged. Paloma must ask children to pay a price. Her POV. Emotional beat: dread of the request.

chapters.title: Asking the Children
chapters.summary: Paloma tells the truth at Ama's table. The children don't flinch; Idris says the dream already took pieces of them, so they'd rather choose what it takes. Ama weeps quietly. Ensemble scene, mostly Idris's POV. Emotional beat: courage that looks like shrugging.

chapters.title: First Key: Idris
chapters.summary: Idris gives his memory of his father's face to the archive. He wakes lighter, unable to mourn properly, and pretends otherwise. Idris's POV. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — what power costs the powerless.

chapters.title: Consortium Sweep
chapters.summary: Enforcers arrive under cover of a 'public health audit,' scanning homes for unregistered electronics. Paloma smuggles the archive core out in a coffin bound for the crematorium. Tense chase chapter, Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: terror sharpened by dark absurdity.

chapters.title: Ama's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ama confronts Voss directly, offering to confess to 'superstition' if he leaves the children alone — buying three days. Voss accepts, because he underestimates grandmothers. Ama's POV. Emotional beat: fierce, sacrificial love.

chapters.title: Second Through Fifth Keys
chapters.summary: Four more children give memories in a candlelit ceremony Sefa rigs to look like a birthday party. Each giving is rendered briefly and devastatingly: a best friend's laugh, a lullaby, a brother, a home address. Rotating child POVs. Emotional beat: cumulative heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Harmonics Rise
chapters.summary: The Consortium intensifies the memory field; adults across the colony begin losing small things — recipes, grievances, the reason they're angry. A convenient amnesia settles over the sector. Sefa's POV documenting it. Emotional beat: horror of soft erasure.

chapters.title: Paloma Forgets Something Important
chapters.summary: Paloma loses twenty minutes and a promise she wrote down herself. She realizes the field is beginning to reach her through years of exposure at the beacon. Her POV, increasingly unreliable narration. Emotional beat: fear of self-loss.

chapters.title: Archive Fragment Two
chapters.summary: A recovered segment reveals Oyelaran survived relocation and became a Consortium archivist — the very system she fled — sabotaging it from within until she was caught. Her final message: 'Deliver it anyway. Especially if it costs you.' Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: communion with a ghost.

chapters.title: Sixth and Seventh Keys
chapters.summary: Two older children give memories that include Paloma herself — picnics, lessons, kindnesses. She attends her own slow disappearance from other minds. Bittersweet ensemble chapter. Emotional beat: found family measured in what it's willing to lose.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Crematorium
chapters.summary: The mortuary attendant, memory-scoured and turned informant, sells the coffin route to Voss. Enforcers seize the decoy core — Sefa built two, but the real one is now exposed in transit. Chase and near-capture, Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: trust wounded.

chapters.title: Eighth Key: Ama
chapters.summary: Ama insists on giving the eighth key despite not being a dreaming child — the Vector accepts her, revealing the ninth key was always meant for an adult who chose to remember. She surrenders her memory of her late husband. Ama's POV. Emotional beat: devotion beyond reason.

chapters.title: Voss Learns What He Guarded
chapters.summary: Voss decrypts the seized decoy and, expecting dissident propaganda, instead hears the Meridian Gate recording — and recognizes his own father's voice authorizing the false attack. Voss's POV, his certainty cracking. Emotional beat: the corrupted confronting their corruption's origin.

chapters.title: The Offer Reversed
chapters.summary: Voss comes to Paloma not with arrest warrants but with a question: 'If I help you, does my name have to be in it?' Paloma must decide whether the man who hunted them deserves mercy. Her POV. Emotional beat: moral fulcrum of the book.

chapters.title: Ninth Key: Paloma
chapters.summary: The Vector names its price: the ninth key must be the maintainer's own dearest memory. Paloma chooses her memory of the found family — every dinner, every name, every night at the table. She gives it before she can lose her nerve. Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: sacrifice as love's final grammar.

chapters.title: Broadcast Night
chapters.summary: Atop the ridge, the children hold hands around the beacon as it wakes fully for the first time in forty years, singing the truth toward every colony in range. Consortium jammers fail against a signal carried on willingly given memory. Climax, rotating POVs. Emotional beat: triumph and terrible emptiness together.

chapters.title: The War Ends Ugly
chapters.summary: Across the sector, the broadcast lands: ceasefires declared, Consortium officials arrested, riots in three domes, celebrations in five. Freedom arrives messy and unfinished. Newsreel-style montage chapter, omniscient-leaning POV. Emotional beat: relief without neatness.

chapters.title: The Stranger on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Paloma wakes with no idea why she climbed the ridge, holding a maintenance log in handwriting she doesn't recognize as hers. The children find her there. They know her; she doesn't know them. Devastating quiet chapter, alternating Paloma and Idris POV. Emotional beat: grief inverted.

chapters.title: Introductions
chapters.summary: The family decides not to tell Paloma what she sacrificed, but simply to let her belong again — Idris teaches her card games she once taught him. Small scenes of re-falling into love with people. Idris's POV. Emotional beat: tenderness as repair.

chapters.title: Voss's Testimony
chapters.summary: Voss testifies publicly, naming his father, ending his family's dynasty. He visits Paloma, who doesn't remember hating him, and finds that almost harder than prosecution. Voss's POV. Emotional beat: accountability without absolution.

chapters.title: What the Children Kept
chapters.summary: The children discover fragments of Paloma survived inside the shared dream — the Vector archived echoes of what she gave. They begin telling her stories of 'a woman who maintained a beacon,' letting her meet herself. Ensemble POV. Emotional beat: memory as communal inheritance.

chapters.title: Recommissioning
chapters.summary: The colony votes to keep the beacon running — openly this time, with a roster of maintainers and a public ledger. Paloma volunteers, feeling drawn to the work without knowing why. Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: vocation as identity surviving memory.

chapters.title: The Dream Changes
chapters.summary: The children's shared dream returns, transformed: no countdown now, just the red star and a voice saying 'thank you' — and, faintly, Paloma's own laughter woven into it. Idris realizes part of her lives in the signal. Idris's POV. Emotional beat: hope with goosebumps.

chapters.title: Yara's Log, Final Entry
chapters.summary: Framed as pages from the pen-name author's discovered journal aboard Sector Nine generations later: the beacon still burns, the story is taught in schools, and a woman's name heads the maintainer roster though no one recalls her face. Epistolary epilogue. Emotional beat: legacy outliving remembrance.

chapters.title: Homecoming Without Maps
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Paloma stands the night watch at the beacon, surrounded by the family she can't remember choosing and chooses again anyway. Idris takes her hand and says, 'You'd like her — the woman who built this.' She believes him. Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: found family, chosen twice.
